circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi designed by Hermann Tilke, serving as the venue for the season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Formula One facility established in the Middle East, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: A street circuit encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb serves as the venue for the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix, along with supporting motorsport events. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 classification, meeting the highest international racing standards.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following modifications and renaming to the A1-Ring, the track returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street-based racing venue situated in Azerbaijan's capital along the Baku Boulevard. At over 6 km in length, it ranks among the longest tracks in Formula One racing. The circuit hosted its first Grand Prix event in 2016 under the European Grand Prix designation, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit, a 5. 412 km facility that opened in 2004, hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, which was the first F1 race staged in the Middle East. Beyond Formula One, the venue accommodates various motorsport disciplines including drag racing, GP2 competition, and 24-hour endurance events, while operating under FIA Grade 1 classification with multiple track configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned as a versatile test of driving ability, featuring an interesting mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit situated in the Walloon region near the town of Spa, which has hosted the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix continuously since 1985 with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006. The venue's history with international motorsport stretches back to 1925, and it featured in the inaugural Formula One season in 1950.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has hosted various international motorsport competitions including sports car championships and North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track additionally accommodates other racing events, including a Formula E championship race that began in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone Circuit, located in Northamptonshire, England, has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably staged the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After rotating among multiple venues throughout the 1950s-1980s, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onward. The track also features on the MotoGP calendar alongside its Formula One commitments.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the site of Formula One's first Eastern Bloc Grand Prix in 1986, constructed in just eight months near a major highway after government plans for a street circuit in the city's main park were rejected. This 4. 381 km track hosted its inaugural race on 24 March 1986, commemorating János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except for a 1980 closure during renovations, and earns its "Temple of Speed" reputation through its characteristic long straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka International Racing Course, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km circuit operated by Honda Mobilityland with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is primarily recognized as a premier venue for Formula One racing and serves as a significant fixture in the international motorsport calendar.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street racing venue located in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through iconic locations along Las Vegas Boulevard. The track passes by prominent casino resorts and entertainment landmarks, including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Mexico City's Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named after two fatal racing drivers from the same family, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The track resumed hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 on its current layout, having previously held the event twice on a different configuration that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that hosts the Miami Grand Prix. The 5. 412-kilometre layout encompasses 19 corners and produces qualifying speeds averaging 224 km/h, designed specifically by Apex Circuit Design for its inaugural Formula One appearance in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, encircling Monaco's harbor. Though officially named after the principality itself, it is widely known by the Monte Carlo designation due to the majority of the circuit running through that particular neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km track hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining the Formula One calendar in 2021, ending a long absence from the championship. The venue's partnership with the sport concludes following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits just north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers, featuring a main straight extending 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal plane crash eight years earlier. The venue hosts major international motorsport events and features an associated kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline, hosting the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural Formula One race in 2021 and recently welcoming electric racing events.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, incorporating portions of both the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Barcelona-Catalunya circuit, located in Montmeló near Barcelona, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test all aspects of driver and car performance. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license, the venue accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix, alongside hosting major events in MotoGP, NASCAR, and World Endurance Championship racing. The venue has attracted numerous international motorsport series over the years, including IndyCar and various sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British driver who represents Thailand in Formula One racing, currently competing for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso represents Aston Martin on the Formula One grid, bringing two World Championship titles earned with Renault in 2005 and 2006, alongside 32 Grand Prix victories accumulated over 23 seasons. Beyond Formula One, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him uniquely the only driver to win both the premier single-seater and world sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, having secured six Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently racing for Haas in Formula One's top tier championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for Audi, competing at the highest level of motorsport competition.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas brings extensive experience to Cadillac's Formula One program, having accumulated 10 race victories throughout his lengthy career in the sport. Previously competing for Mercedes, he achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the championship standings during 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto, an Argentine motorsport competitor, currently races in Formula One as a member of the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian motorsport competitor who races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with Nielsen Racing, while maintaining a reserve driver position at Haas in Formula One. During the 2024-2025 seasons, he made seven Grand Prix starts for the team.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One competitor currently driving for Alpine, who previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020 while representing AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One while driving for Red Bull Racing, though he holds dual French and Algerian citizenship.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured seven world championship titles that equal Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple performance records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium appearances in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One and has achieved significant success beyond the sport's premier series, most notably capturing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche in endurance racing.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls. He has established himself as a professional racing driver competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, races for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has secured nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen has transitioned to sports car and stock car racing after his Formula One career, which spanned 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. He currently competes as a factory driver for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship while maintaining a part-time commitment to NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, claimed the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025 after competing in the sport for eight seasons. The 2025 title victory marks his most significant achievement alongside his 12 Grand Prix victories accumulated throughout his career.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One, having previously secured a Grand Prix victory with Alpine at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing in Formula One for Cadillac. The experienced competitor finished as runner-up in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his 15-season career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver for McLaren, has claimed nine Formula One victories during his time in the sport. He has achieved these wins across four racing seasons in the championship.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his 14-season tenure in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having accumulated seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has claimed four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous experience in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver who currently races for Aston Martin in the sport's top championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda raced in Formula One across five seasons from 2021 through 2025, currently holding a reserve driver position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver races for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season career, Verstappen has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the championship between 2022 and 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the series.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated as Renault's official Formula One entry until rebranding as Alpine in 2021 to represent the French sports car marque, before Renault's departure from the sport at the end of 2025. Competing with Mercedes power units, Alpine secured its only victory through Esteban Ocon at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, with the squad now fielding Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto as its driver pairing.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple team entities, with its current racing operation trading as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team under AMR GP Limited ownership.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, competing continuously since the championship's 1950 inception. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the team has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire modern history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One outfit in 2014, with the team launching its competitive campaign in 2016. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the organization as team principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner who held the position since the team's establishment before departing in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss engineering firm Sauber, established in 1970, competed as an independent Formula One constructor from 1993 onward while also achieving notable success in endurance racing, including a Le Mans victory in 1989. Following numerous structural changes over three decades, the team concluded its racing operations in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-running constructors before being acquired by Audi to serve as the foundation for their F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One team headquartered at its technology facility in Woking, operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under majority ownership by Mumtalakat Holding Company. The outfit competes in the championship under a naming rights partnership arrangement.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 in both manufacturing and team operations, currently competing from their Brackley headquarters under the Mercedes-AMG Petronas banner with a German licence. The team underwent ownership restructuring in 2022 when Ineos acquired an equal one-third stake alongside the Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff, each holding equivalent control. Mercedes-branded racing operations have earned the historic designation "Silver Arrows" throughout their involvement in the sport.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister team within the Red Bull motorsport structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competition in 2024, operating as a sister team to Red Bull Racing under Austrian ownership. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the squad represents Red Bull GmbH's second constructor entry in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England, has been a dominant force in the sport since its 2005 establishment under the ownership of Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the team through two decades of success before Laurent Mekies assumed the management role in 2025, while the conglomerate also operates a second F1 team through Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging after Williams's prior failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name and has established itself as a significant presence in the sport's history.
